heading: Anxiety and autistic traits in adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis
text: The study did not find a significant overall association and found extraordinarily high heterogeneity between studies.
notProven: It is particularly useful for avoiding the presentation of an autism–anxiety correlation as uniform across non-clinical samples.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis with 18 independent samples from 13 studies. It is particularly useful for avoiding the presentation of an autism–anxiety correlation as uniform across non-clinical samples.

heading: Prevalence of Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) in autistic children or young people and adults: A systematic review and meta-analysis
sample: 17 studies of children/young people (53,918) and 13 adult studies (142,081)
text: Prevalence estimates based on diagnostic criteria were lower than many estimates obtained from symptom scales alone.
notProven: There may be under-detection when tools are not adapted; not every traumatic experience is PTSD.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis with 17 studies of children/young people (53,918) and 13 adult studies (142,081). There may be under-detection when tools are not adapted; not every traumatic experience is PTSD.

heading: The Assessment and Treatment of Post-traumatic Stress Disorder in Autistic People: A Systematic Review
sample: Literature on assessment and treatment of PTSD in autistic people
text: The study reviews limitations in assessment and the small evidence base for adapted treatments.
notProven: It does not support claiming that a well-established autism-specific PTSD protocol with robust evidence already exists.
linea: Systematic review. It does not support claiming that a well-established autism-specific PTSD protocol with robust evidence already exists.

heading: The Co-Occurrence of Autism and Avoidant/Restrictive Food Intake Disorder (ARFID): A Prevalence-Based Meta-Analysis
text: The study found mutual over-representation of autism and ARFID, but with wide intervals and substantial heterogeneity.
notProven: It does not show that ARFID is 'part of autism' or that selective eating is ARFID.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis with 21 studies and 7,442 participants. It does not show that ARFID is 'part of autism' or that selective eating is ARFID.

heading: Investigating the Presence of Autistic Traits and Prevalence of Autism Spectrum Disorder Symptoms in Anorexia Nervosa: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
sample: 22 studies; 1,172 patients with anorexia and 2,747 controls
text: The study found more autistic traits in anorexia and a modest correlation with eating-disorder severity.
notProven: A screening score above a cut-off is not the same as an autism diagnosis; clinical overlap complicates interpretation.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis with 22 studies, 1,172 patients with anorexia and 2,747 controls. A screening score above a cut-off is not the same as an autism diagnosis; clinical overlap complicates interpretation.

heading: A Mixed Method Systematic Review Into the Impact of ED Treatment in Autistic People and Those With High Autistic Traits
sample: Studies of eating-disorder treatment in autistic people or people with high autistic traits
text: The study identifies treatment barriers and outcomes that may differ when autism or a high level of autistic traits is present.
notProven: The evidence remains heterogeneous and does not establish one adaptation that is effective for every eating disorder.
linea: Mixed-methods systematic review. The evidence remains heterogeneous and does not establish one adaptation that is effective for every eating disorder.

heading: The search for gastrointestinal inflammation in autism: a systematic review and meta-analysis of non-invasive gastrointestinal markers
text: The study evaluates whether there is consistent evidence of gastrointestinal inflammation using non-invasive markers.
notProven: It does not support attributing gastrointestinal symptoms to one inflammatory cause or using experimental biomarkers as an autism diagnosis.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis. It does not support attributing gastrointestinal symptoms to one inflammatory cause or using experimental biomarkers as an autism diagnosis.

heading: Ameliorating Gastrointestinal Symptoms in Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder by Modulating the Gut Microbiota: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
sample: Trials of prebiotics, probiotics, synbiotics and faecal transplantation
text: The study analyses effects on gastrointestinal symptoms and the gut microbiota in autistic children.
notProven: The trial base is limited and heterogeneous; it does not justify broadly recommending microbiota treatments.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis. The trial base is limited and heterogeneous; it does not justify broadly recommending microbiota treatments.

heading: Autism in patients with eosinophilic gastrointestinal disease: A systematic review with meta-analysis
text: The study examines reported co-occurrence between autism and eosinophilic gastrointestinal diseases.
notProven: An epidemiological association does not imply a causal relationship or justify indiscriminate screening.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis. An epidemiological association does not imply a causal relationship or justify indiscriminate screening.

heading: Pain assessment for children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorders (ASD): A systematic review
text: The study reviews pain-assessment tools and pain responses in autistic children and adolescents, including difficulties when spoken communication does not accurately reflect the experience.
notProven: There is no single behavioural expression of pain that is valid for every autistic person.
linea: Systematic review. There is no single behavioural expression of pain that is valid for every autistic person.

heading: Menstruation and Autism: a qualitative systematic review
text: The study describes physical, emotional and social impacts and identifies differences between the priorities of autistic people, families and professionals.
notProven: The literature is small and describes sample diversity poorly; experiences cannot be universalised.
linea: Qualitative systematic review with 12 sources (8 peer-reviewed, 4 grey literature). The literature is small and describes sample diversity poorly; experiences cannot be universalised.

heading: Clinical characteristics of children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder and epilepsy: a systematic review and meta-analysis
text: Epilepsy occurs in a relevant minority of autistic people and its frequency varies with age, intellectual disability and other characteristics.
notProven: It is not accurate to use one figure for the entire autistic population or to assume causation.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis with 66 studies from 53 articles. It is not accurate to use one figure for the entire autistic population or to assume causation.

heading: Factors associated with the occurrence of epilepsy in autism: a systematic review
sample: 53 studies; up to 257,892 participants in prevalence studies
text: The study identifies intellectual/cognitive disability as one of the factors most consistently associated with epilepsy in autism.
notProven: Only a minority of studies were high quality; associated factors are not necessarily causal.
linea: Systematic review with 53 studies and up to 257,892 participants in prevalence studies. Only a minority of studies were high quality; associated factors are not necessarily causal.

heading: Clinical sequencing yield in epilepsy, autism spectrum disorder, and intellectual disability: A systematic review and meta-analysis
text: The study estimated different diagnostic yields of genetic sequencing in autism, epilepsy and intellectual disability.
notProven: Diagnostic yields depend heavily on clinical selection and access, and the studies are geographically biased.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis with 103 studies and 32,331 participants. Diagnostic yields depend heavily on clinical selection and access, and the studies are geographically biased.

heading: Comparing Executive Functions in Children and Adolescents with Autism and ADHD-A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
sample: Studies of autism, ADHD and co-occurrence
text: The study compares executive-function profiles and shows that the result also depends on whether performance tests or questionnaires about everyday functioning are used.
notProven: It does not allow autism, ADHD or AuDHD to be diagnosed using an executive-function task.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis. It does not allow autism, ADHD or AuDHD to be diagnosed using an executive-function task.

heading: The efficacy of executive function interventions in children with autism spectrum disorder: a systematic review and meta-analysis
text: The study finds signals of improvement in executive functions after certain interventions.
notProven: The diversity of interventions and measures prevents assuming that any form of 'brain training' is effective.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis. The diversity of interventions and measures prevents assuming that any form of 'brain training' is effective.

heading: Autism spectrum disorders: a meta-analysis of executive function
text: The study found broad, moderate group differences in executive function, but low diagnostic sensitivity of the measures.
notProven: Executive difficulties are not universal and cannot by themselves diagnose autism.
linea: Meta-analysis with 235 studies and 14,081 participants. Executive difficulties are not universal and cannot by themselves diagnose autism.

heading: Autistic traits are associated with lower perceived executive function but not poorer executive function task performance in the general population: complementary meta-analytic evidence
text: The study separates perceived everyday executive difficulties from performance on executive-function tasks, which do not show the same pattern.
notProven: This is general-population research on traits, not a clinical autistic sample; it should not be directly extrapolated.
linea: Meta-analysis. This is general-population research on traits, not a clinical autistic sample; it should not be directly extrapolated.

heading: Comparison of Physical Activity Between Children With and Without Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
text: The study found lower average physical activity in autistic children than in non-autistic children.
notProven: It does not explain why the difference exists and does not imply a lack of interest in sport.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis with 31 studies. It does not explain why the difference exists and does not imply a lack of interest in sport.

heading: Benefits of exercise for children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder: a systematic review and meta-analysis
sample: Trials/interventions in autistic children and adolescents
text: The study summarises the effects of exercise programmes on several physical and psychosocial outcomes.
notProven: Programmes are heterogeneous and not every outcome has the same level of certainty.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis. Programmes are heterogeneous and not every outcome has the same level of certainty.
